one_liner: Research code on 2016-era TBLIS: tensor contractions via one- or two-level Strassen, up to 1.3x over regular TBLIS.
what_it_does: Speeds up large tensor contractions (C += A*B over arbitrary index bundles) by applying Strassen's algorithm without first transposing the tensors into matrices. The API mirrors the old TBLIS interface: tblis::stra_mult and stra_mult_2level take the same (alpha, A, idx_A, B, idx_B, beta, C, idx_C) arguments as tblis::mult, and there is a matrix version as well (stra_mult, stra_mult_ab, stra_mult_naive on matrix views). It ships with a test_strassen driver, scripts for the TCCG Tensor Contraction Benchmark (tcb.txt), and MPI scripts for distributed runs.
how_it_is_fast: It uses the Block-Scatter-Matrix layout to treat a tensor contraction as a GEMM on general-stride storage, so Strassen's 7-multiply recursion runs on the tensors in place, with no explicit permutation and no extra workspace (README). It adapts the authors' earlier BLIS-based Strassen-for-GEMM implementation (linked in the README): operand sums are folded into packing, and the default 'ABC' variant uses dedicated AVX micro-kernels (bli_dstra_asm_8x4 plus 'two' and 'four' variants) that write several C sub-blocks in one pass. 'AB' and 'Naive' variants are included for comparison. Each Strassen level does 7 block multiplies instead of 8, which is where the up-to-1.3x gain at large sizes comes from.
when_to_use: Research or reproduction of the SISC 2018 Strassen-for-tensor-contraction results on an x86 machine with AVX.
Very large double-precision contractions with big free and contracted dimensions (the square sweep runs 256 to 20480), where 1-2 Strassen levels can beat a conventional GEMM-based contraction.
As a reference implementation of the Block-Scatter-Matrix plus fused-Strassen-packing technique for porting into a modern TBLIS or BLIS build.
Distributed-memory contraction experiments on a SLURM cluster, using the bundled dist/ scripts as a starting point.
when_not_to_use: Production code: no commits since 2017-07-07, and it fails to compile with GCC 10.3 (open issue #1, 'B is not a constant expression' in stra_matrify.hpp).

Single precision or complex data: optimized Strassen micro-kernels exist only for double (bli_dstra_asm_8x4 and its two- and four-output variants) in the sandybridge config. The float and complex Strassen slots are left empty.
Modern CPUs with AVX2/AVX-512: the documented build is --enable-config=sandybridge (AVX, 8x4 double kernel), so FMA hardware is not used by the Strassen path.
Small or skinny contractions: Strassen's extra additions only pay off at large sizes. The paper reports gains of at most 1.3x.
Code that needs bit-for-bit agreement with a conventional contraction: Strassen reorders the floating-point arithmetic, and the driver reports a norm-2 error against the regular TBLIS result.

integration.dependencies: A 2016-era TBLIS with BLIS-derived kernels in the tree, and TCI threading (tci.h). Build needs autotools (autoreconf). OpenMP runtime for the driver (omp_get_wtime, OMP_NUM_THREADS/KMP_AFFINITY). Optional BLAS, hwloc and memkind are detected by configure. mvapich2 2.1 and SLURM for the distributed experiments.
integration.min_toolchain: C99 and C++11. Authors used icc/icpc 15.0.3 with the GCC 4.9.3 standard library. GCC 10.3 is reported to fail (issue #1).
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX (artifact: 'x86-64 processor that supports AVX instructions'), Linux or macOS. Strassen kernels only in the sandybridge config.
integration.thread_safety: not documented. The Strassen variant (ABC/AB/Naive) is picked through the process-global tblis::internal::impl, so concurrent callers cannot use different variants safely. Parallelism comes from TCI with BLIS_*_NT and OpenMP environment variables.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — stra_mult has the same signature as the bundled TBLIS mult, but that is the 2016 TBLIS API, not current MatthewsResearchGroup/tblis, so moving to this code base means replacing TBLIS.

gotchas: Only 1 or 2 Strassen levels: stra_mult and stra_mult_2level. The driver prints 'More than 2-level is not supported' for L>2.
Variant selection is a global setting (tblis::internal::impl = BLIS_BASED / STRA_AB / STRA_NAIVE), not a function argument.
The bin/*_run_*.sh scripts write results with plain 'tee', not 'tee -a', so each line overwrites the .m result file. Capture stdout instead.
The timing harness allocates two 100M-double cache-flush buffers (about 1.7 GB) on every timed call and reports best-of-niter (default 3) effective GFLOPS = 2mnk/time.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over TBLIS (MatthewsResearchGroup/tblis) only when you are studying or porting Strassen for tensor contraction: TBLIS is the maintained, multi-architecture code base but has no Strassen path. For plain matrices, fmm-gen (also from the FLAME group) and fast-matmul (Benson and Ballard) cover a wider family of fast algorithms against a conventional GEMM or MKL.
verified_claims_summary: The authors' peer-reviewed SISC 2018 paper (README abstract) reports up to 1.3x effective GFLOPS over the same code's regular TBLIS contraction (L=0), measured on synthetic contractions and the TCCG benchmark on single-core, multicore and distributed runs. Those runs used icc 15.0.3, the Sandy Bridge AVX double-precision kernels and TACC Maverick (CPU model not stated). Per-case numbers are in the paper, which was not opened, so only the 'up to' figure is confirmed.
status_note: Abandoned research artifact (last commit 2017-07-07, one open build-failure issue). BSD-3-Clause (TBLIS's license, copyright Devin Matthews), so copyable, but expect to patch it for modern compilers.
